sessionExpiresAt.description: ISO 8601 timestamp at which the current session expires. Used by the frontend to proactively prompt re-authentication before the hard cutoff.

dailyLimitReached.description: Whether the user has spent their plan's daily LLM budget. Free plan only; always false on paid plans, which have no daily allowance.

usedPct.description: Percent of today's allowance already spent, 0-100 and clamped at 100. Deliberately a percentage rather than the underlying microcents: the raw figure is a provider cost we do not want to publish per-user, and a percentage is the only honest unit for an allowance shared across models with different prices.

resetsAt.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of the next allowance reset. Computed server-side because the window is the UTC calendar day, which is 01:00/02:00 local for this product's German audience — the client must render this rather than assume its own midnight.

freeUsage.description: Today's allowance usage, or null on plans with no daily allowance. Lets the UI warn before the wall instead of only reporting it after.

creditBalanceMicro.description: Remaining credit pool balance in microcents (TEAM only).

quotaExhausted.description: Whether the user's model access is restricted due to quota/overage limits.

subscriptionStatus.description: Raw Stripe subscription_status (active, trialing, past_due, unpaid, canceled, etc.). Null for free plans.

isPartnerOrg.description: Whether the organization is reseller-managed by a partner (billing handled offline, no Stripe). True only for the 'reseller' billing relationship.

capabilities.description: The Layer-1 capabilities this user holds, resolved user > team > org_default. Lets an affordance react BEFORE the user reaches a screen that asks for input — a denied user previously filled in a whole connect wizard, credential included, and learned of the refusal only on submit. Any key an org has authored no explicit denial for reports true; org admins are resolved like everybody else, since the matrix binds them too. The server stays the authority — this payload never grants anything, it only lets the UI stop asking.

billingRelationship.description: How the org's billing is owned: 'direct' (self-serve, Stripe), 'reseller' (partner-managed, billed offline), or 'affiliate' (direct-Stripe org attributed to a partner).

Start device authorization for a desktop client.
post.description: Begins the device authorization flow (RFC 8628 style). The client generates a random secret locally, sends only its SHA-256 hash here, and keeps the raw secret to authenticate the later token poll. Returns the codes and the browser verification URL. No credential is ever placed in the URL.

userCode.description: Short code the user enters in the browser.

interval.description: Seconds to wait between token polls.

post.summary: Poll a device authorization for its session token.
post.description: Polled by the desktop client until the user approves in the browser. The raw device secret is sent in the X-Device-Secret header, never in the URL. Returns status 'pending' until approved, then 'complete' with a one-time session token.

parameters.description: Raw device secret matching the secretHash sent to /device.

schema.description: Raw device secret matching the secretHash sent to /device.

token.description: Session token, present only when status is 'complete'.

usage.description: Display-only per-turn cost/token/duration summary for this assistant message. Computed off the billing path from the same usage + pricing the gateway billed. Present only on assistant messages produced after the feature landed.

autoRouted.description: True when Auto Routing chose this assistant message's model.

branches.description: List of branches that start at this message, i.e. alternatives to the current message. Also includes the currently selected branch ID.

name.description: Full name, or the email when no name is set.

author.description: Who typed this message. Present on user messages sent after the feature landed, and on user messages backfilled from the chat's owner. placeholder.description: The token that replaced the span in the stored message.

patternTitle.description: Title of the pattern that triggered the redaction.

redactions.description: Compliance redactions applied to this user message. Present only when the message had sensitive spans replaced; lets the frontend restore the original text inline.

isBlocked.description: Whether the chat has been blocked due to compliance violations.

isOwner.description: Whether the current user may write this chat in place — owns it AND holds write on its project.

ownerName.description: Display name of `chats.user_id` — the one person who may append to this chat. Shown in the header when the reader is not that person.

canFork.description: Whether sending a message will copy the chat instead of appending to it. True for anyone who can read it but not write it.

forksToPersonalProject.description: Where a fork would land. TRUE when the caller cannot write the chat's project, so the copy goes to their personal project rather than staying put. Meaningless unless `canFork`.

spaceId.description: The project the copy lives in.

myForks.description: Copies of THIS chat that the calling user already owns, newest first. Forking repeatedly is intended — but without this the user cannot see they have already done it, and makes another copy they did not mean to. Empty for a chat the caller has never forked, and for a chat that is not forkable.

suggestions.description: Follow-up question suggestions generated after the last assistant turn. Empty for chats that haven't produced a turn since the feature was added.

get.summary: List the caller's pending AI edit suggestions for an artifact.
get.description:
Returns only suggestions that are PENDING, belong to the calling
user, and are visible on the branch their originating chat is currently on.

Branch visibility is a join rather than a stored flag: a suggestion records the
CHUNK it was produced in, and a chunk is inherited by every branch descended from
it, truncated at that branch's `up_to`. So editing a message away drops its
suggestions from the answer here, and paging back to the original branch brings
them back — with no delete path and nothing to keep in sync.

Unpaginated by design: the set is bounded by what one turn can propose against
one document, and the client renders all of it at once anyway.

patch.summary: Accept or reject one AI edit suggestion.
patch.description:
Records the caller's decision. Terminal and one-way: only a
PENDING suggestion can be resolved, and a resolved one cannot be reopened — a
reopen would let a later request re-offer a change the user already applied to the
document, which is the resurrection bug this table exists to prevent.

Accepting does NOT edit the document. The edit is a Yjs mutation the client makes
over the collab socket, which has its own write gate, and the client only records
the accept once the document has taken it. Recording it here as well would create
a second authority for one decision, free to disagree with the first.
